identity.title: The ALMA detection of CO rotational line emission in AGB stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud

paper_type_evidence.quote: The Atacama Large Millimeter Array was used to observe 2 OH/IR stars and 4 carbon stars in the LMC in the CO J= 2-1 line.

distance_source.value: assumed 50 kpc in the gas MLR formula

question.value: Can CO thermal line emission be spectrally resolved in AGB stars in the LMC, giving expansion velocities and mass-loss rates to compare with Galactic stars and wind theory?

evidence.quote: Attempt to, for the first time, spectrally resolve CO thermal line emission in a small sample of AGB stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00319.S.
The sources were observed with ALMA at Band 6 on 2015 January 18, 19, and April 9 using 34, 41, and 35 12m antennas, respectively.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Line SPW 937.5 MHz, 3840 channels centred on 230.303 GHz; three 2 GHz continuum windows (128 channels) at 212.791, 214.789, 227.782 GHz

evidence.quote: The line spectral window was centered on 230.303 GHz, and the continuum windows were centered on 212.791, 214.789, and 227.782 GHz.
observe 2 OH/IR stars and 4 carbon stars in the LMC in the CO J= 2-1 line.
using 34, 41, and 35 12m antennas, respectively.
The observations covered a baseline range of $\sim15-350$ m providing a maximum recoverable scale of $\sim10.5\ensuremath{''}$.
the typical beam size is $1.7\ensuremath{''}\times1.2\ensuremath{''}$, at a position angle of $\sim$$80^\circ$.
providing a maximum recoverable scale of $\sim10.5\ensuremath{''}$.

sensitivity.value: continuum rms ~45 uJy/beam; line rms 3.1-4.1 mJy/beam (1 km/s channels)

evidence.quote: The typical rms noise in the continuum images is $\sim$45$\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ and that in the line maps ranges from $3.1-4.1$ mJy beam$^{-1}$.

time_on_source.value: 3.9 hrs total, of which 2.1 hrs spread equally over six sources

evidence.quote: The total observing time was 3.9 hrs of which 2.1 hrs were spread equally over the six sources.
The sources were observed with ALMA at Band 6 on 2015 January 18, 19, and April 9

analysis_steps.goal: Extract line profiles and fit expansion/stellar velocities

method.value: Spectra from area ~twice the beam, converted to temperature scale; fitted with CLASS Shell profile

evidence.quote: Line profiles were extracted from an area typically twice the beam-size and converted to a temperature scale within CASA.
$H$ was fixed to $-1$ in the fitting.

assumptions.value: OH/IR star velocities fixed to OH values due to low S/N

evidence.quote: were fixed to the values determined from OH observations (Goldman et al. 2016) because of the poor signal-to-noise ratio

fitting.value: Shell profile fit; v_exp = half the full width at zero intensity

evidence.quote: the expansion velocity v$_{\rm exp}$ is taken as half that value

validation.value: For IRAS 05506 H left free gave H = -1.02 +/- 0.02

evidence.quote: we also fitted a profile allowing this parameter to vary as well and found $H= -1.02 \pm 0.02$.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive dust-driven-wind MLR and gas-to-dust ratio

method.value: Modified MoD with DUSTY density type = 3; r_gd chosen so predicted v_exp equals observed

evidence.quote: One can then compare this predicted expansion velocity to the observed value and determine the gas-to-dust ratio that makes them equal

evidence.quote: The fitted parameters are luminosity, dust optical depth, and dust temperature at the inner radius.

results_numeric.quantity: Gas-to-dust ratios of LMC C-stars (IRAS 05506, 05125, ERO 0529379, ERO 0518117)

evidence.quote: while that for the 4 LMC C-stars is 11.4 km s$^{-1}$

results_numeric.quantity: Median v_exp of Galactic C-stars with L>5400 Lsun

evidence.quote: The median value of the expansion velocity of the stars with luminosities above 5400 L$_{\odot}$ (the lowest of the LMC stars) is 17.6 km s$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: All four C-stars detected in CO 2-1; only one of two OH/IR stars detected (marginally)

evidence.quote: All 4 C stars are detected, and one of the two OH/IR stars.

findings_qualitative.value: CO-based gas MLRs fall below dust-based MLRs, by factor 4-5 for C-stars and >20 for OH/IR stars

evidence.quote: For the OH/IR stars the discrepancy is a factor $>$ 20, for the C-stars it is a factor of $4-5$

claims.hypothesis: Expansion velocities of C-star winds are lower in the LMC than in the solar neighbourhood
claims.experiment: Measured v_exp from ALMA CO 2-1 and compared to Galactic standard and extreme C-stars
claims.result: LMC median 11.4 km/s vs 17.6 km/s for comparable Galactic stars
claims.finding: Lower metallicity gives smaller expansion velocity with similar MLR, consistent with Wachter et al. models

evidence.quote: it seems consistent with the finding for the Galactic halo C-stars that the expansion velocities are smaller at lower metallicity.

claims.hypothesis: LMC C-star MLRs are similar to those of Galactic extreme C-stars
claims.experiment: DUSTY density type 3 modelling of LMC and Galactic samples
claims.result: MLRs of the four stars very similar and in agreement with Galactic extreme C-stars

evidence.quote: The MLRs of the four stars turn out to be very similar and in agreement with the MLRs found for the Galactic extreme C-stars.

claims.hypothesis: The Galactic CO-intensity formula predicts LMC gas MLRs correctly
claims.experiment: Applied Ramstedt & Olofsson formula and compared to dust MLRs
claims.finding: Possible CO abundance overestimate, time-variable mass loss, or stronger ISRF

evidence.quote: Gas MLRs derived from a simple formula are significantly smaller than derived from the dust modelling

why_this_data.value: Maximum baseline chosen so emission stays unresolved given expected CO photodissociation radius

evidence.quote: The maximum baseline (and thus the size of the beam) was chosen to match the expected CO photodissociation radius based on the formula of Mamon et al. (1988) so that the emission region remains unresolved.

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample and non-trivial comparison with Galactic stars due to distance uncertainties

evidence.quote: It must be stressed, however, that our sample is small and finding a suitable sample of comparison stars in the Galaxy is challenging.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only four C-star detections; statistics weak
Gas-to-dust ratios degenerate with assumed distance and grain density
Detailed CO radiative transfer deferred, so the MLR discrepancy is not resolved
